title: Quasi-projective morphisms compose over a quasi-compact base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $S$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] that are respectively $f$-relatively ample and $g$-relatively ample. Then $g\circ f$ is of finite type and there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $N$ that is $(g\circ f)$-relatively ample. Here an invertible module $L$ on the source of a morphism $h$ is $h$-relatively ample if $h$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and, for every affine open $V$ of its target, $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].
